title: Subgroup and Submonoid Membership in the lampshuffler of $\mathbb{Z}$
summary: The lampshuffler group of $\mathbb{Z}$ is the semidirect product $\operatorname{FSym}(\mathbb{Z}) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}$, which consists of all permutations of $\mathbb{Z}$ that act as a translation outside a finite set. This infinite permutation group naturally contains as subgroups the wreath products $H \wr \mathbb{Z}$ for every finite group $H$. We prove that the Subgroup Membership Problem, and more generally, the Submonoid Membership Problem, are decidable in $\operatorname{FSym}(\mathbb{Z}) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}$.
